title: Finite affine comparison of geometric and scalar adjunction counits
statement: Let f:X -> Y be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] between Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let A=f_*O_X, g:(X,O_X) -> (Y,A) [def-sc-direct-image-algebra-derived-category], and assume D(O_X), D(O_Y), and D(A) exist [def-pc-derived-category]. Let R:D_QCoh(X) -> D_QCoh(Y), comparison:R followed by inclusion ≅ inclusion followed by Rf_* [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and adj:R ⊣ a be specified. Let rho:D(A) -> D(O_Y) be the chosen right derived scalar restriction and adjA:rho ⊣ rhoR a specified ambient adjunction. For K in D_QCoh(Y), assume both K and a(K) are bounded below. There exist a natural isomorphism c:Rg_* followed by rho ≅ Rf_* on the entire D(O_X) [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] and an isomorphism phi:Rg_*(a(K)) ≅ rhoR(K) in D(A), such that c_{a(K)}.inv followed by rho(phi.hom) followed by adjA.counit_K equals comparison_{a(K)}.inv followed by the underlying morphism of adj.counit_K. This asserts no internal-Hom identification and no evaluation formula.

proof.text: Obtain the whole-derived-category factorization c from lem-sc-finite-affine-derived-factorization.

Use the functor comparison of finite_affine_derived_equivalence to show T=inclusion_X followed by Rg_* is fully faithful. Quasi-coherence of rhoR(K) from lem-sc-finite-scalar-right-adjoint-qcoh makes it an object B of D_QCoh(A). Take N=E.inverse(B); the comparison and the equivalence counit give T(N) ≅ rhoR(K).

Whisker c inverse with inclusion_X and compose with the specified comparison to obtain beta:R followed by inclusion_Y ≅ T followed by rho. Put u=beta inverse at a(K) followed by inclusion_Y of the geometric counit, and g=adjA.homEquiv(u). For each M, full faithfulness of T, the geometric adjunction, full faithfulness of inclusion_Y and beta give a composite Hom equivalence q. Naturality of beta and the counit formula prove q(h)=adjA.homEquiv.symm(h followed by g). Hence postcomposition by g is bijective on Hom(T(M),T(a(K))). Apply surjectivity at N to the isomorphism e:T(N) ≅ rhoR(K), obtaining v with v followed by g=e.hom. Set t=e.inv followed by v. Then t followed by g=id; injectivity at a(K) gives g followed by t=id. Thus phi=asIso(g), with rho(phi.hom) followed by the ambient counit=u. Expand beta inverse and cancel c inverse followed by c hom to obtain exactly the required counit equation. No boundedness of a(K), global restriction of a, or t-exactness is used.
